key_insight: Friction stir welding with in-situ Al2O3 reinforcement improved the joint quality of AA2014-T6/AA5083-H111, boosting strength, hardness, and wear resistance.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a practical route to strengthen dissimilar aluminium welds by combining groove-filling reinforcement with multi-pass friction stir processing.
method: Machined a single 45° V-groove along the dissimilar aluminium joint.
Inserted Al2O3 particles into the groove and applied three friction stir processing passes.
Evaluated microhardness, tensile behavior, wear performance, SEM/EDS mapping, and fracture morphology.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stir-zone hardness up to 105 VHN, tensile strength gains of up to 18% over the unreinforced joint, and the lowest wear rate at 9 wt.% Al2O3.
watch_item: The benefits depend on uniform particle dispersion and process control; excessive or uneven reinforcement could compromise weld consistency.
paper_title: Analysis of tensile properties, fracture characteristics, and microstructural features in friction stir welding of dissimilar aluminium alloys reinforced with Al 2 O 3
